subject: Music
examFormat: The syllabus aims to prepare candidates for the Board's UTME in Music. Its course objectives are to: appreciate and discuss music fairly and critically; identify, through written/aural analysis, the features of the music of different periods of Western and African music theory history, peoples, its forms and the media; appreciate the influence of socio-cultural and technological factors on the lives and music of musicians; and attain a sound musical basis for further learning at the tertiary level. The syllabus is arranged in five sections: A Rudiments of Music, B Elementary Harmony, C History and Literature of African Music, D History and Literature of Western Music, E Comparative Music Studies.

topics.name: The staff
objectives: identify all the components of the staff and their application
topics.content: Great staff; ledger lines and spaces; open score (vocal score); C clef, alto (viola clef) and tenor clef.

topics.name: Music notes and rests and their values
objectives: determine the relative duration of different notes and rests
topics.content: Music notes/rests and their corresponding values.

topics.name: Time and time signatures
objectives: interpret varied rhythmic patterns
topics.content: Simple and compound time signatures; the correct grouping of notes and barring of unbarred passages.

topics.name: Key signatures and scales
objectives: ascertain names of the various degrees of the diatonic scales
identify simple scale passages with or without key signature
topics.content: A: technical names of the various degrees of the scale; diatonic major/minor (natural, harmonic and melodic); chromatic scales. B: determination of the key of a piece of music with or without key signature not exceeding two sharps and two flats.

topics.name: Keyboard setting, enharmonic equivalents and accidentals
objectives: identify the names of the white and black keys and their relationship, e.g. C sharp = D flat, B sharp = C
topics.content: Keyboard setting and enharmonic equivalents; accidentals.

topics.name: Intervals
objectives: determine different qualities of intervals (melodic and harmonic)
topics.content: Recognition of diatonic/chromatic intervals and their inversions (e.g. perfect unison, perfect 4th, perfect 5th, perfect 8ve), major/minor 2nd, 3rd, 6th and 7th, diminished 5th and augmented 4th; recognition of consonant and dissonant intervals.

topics.name: Musical terms, signs and abbreviations
objectives: interpret simple musical signs and terms
topics.content: Definition of simple musical terms, signs and abbreviations.

topics.name: Transcription and transposition
objectives: read music in any given notation
rewrite a music passage on a given stave
topics.content: Transcription of music from staff into tonic solfa notation and vice-versa; transposition using the treble (G) and bass (F) staves not exceeding two sharps and two flats.

topics.name: Triads and their inversions
objectives: identify triads
compare types of triads
determine the use of triads
topics.content: Triads and their inversions in major/minor keys, not exceeding two sharps and two flats: primary triads in major keys; secondary triads in major keys. Chord indications: major triads are indicated with capital Roman numerals (e.g. I), minor triads with small Roman numerals (e.g. ii), diminished triads with small Roman numerals with an 'o' sign (e.g. vii o), augmented triads with capital numerals with a '+' (e.g. III+). In any major scale the major triads are I, IV and V, the minor triads are ii, iii and vi, and the diminished triad is vii o. In any harmonic minor the minor triads are i and iv, the major triads are V and VI, the diminished triads are ii o and vii o, and the augmented triad is III+. Primary triads are I, IV and V in major scales but i, iv and V in harmonic minor scales.

topics.name: Chord progressions and the dominant 7th chord
objectives: determine the basic chord progressions in a music passage
recognize the dominant 7th chord
topics.content: Basic chord progressions in four-part vocal style (SATB) in major keys not exceeding two sharps and two flats; dominant 7th chord in root position only.

topics.name: Kinds of motion
objectives: identify the various kinds of motion in a musical passage
topics.content: Parallel, similar, contrary and oblique.

topics.name: Cadences
objectives: identify the various types of cadences in a musical score
topics.content: Cadences in major keys not exceeding two sharps and two flats: perfect/full close cadence; imperfect/half close/semi cadence; plagal/Amen cadence; interrupted/deceptive/evaded/surprise cadence.

topics.name: Non-harmonic tones
objectives: relate harmonic or non-harmonic tones to the chords with which they are associated
topics.content: Identification and application of neighbouring tones/auxiliary notes and passing tones/notes.

topics.name: Modulation
objectives: determine the key of a given melody and its modulation
topics.content: Simple diatonic modulations (using a single melodic line) from any given major key not exceeding two sharps and two flats to any of its closely related keys (dominant and subdominant).

topics.name: Elementary composition
objectives: identify suitable melody to given words, compatible, balanced or contrasting phrases
topics.content: Setting of words to written melody; recognition of suitable answers to given musical phrases.

topics.name: Nigerian folksongs
objectives: identify various folksongs and their types
define and compare their forms and features
topics.content: Types, forms and characteristics. Types: cradle, folk-tales, games, war, satirical, dirges/funeral, historical, praise and worksong, etc. Forms: call and response, strophic, through-composed, antiphony, etc. Characteristics: vocal styles (recitative, yodeling, ululation, incantation, heaving, whistling, nasalisation, etc); scales/modes (tritonic, tetratonic, pentatonic, hexatonic, etc); metre/rhythm (metric and non-metric, polymetric, cross rhythm, syncopation, hemiola, poly-rhythm, etc).

topics.name: Nigerian traditional music and other arts
objectives: analyse the features and forms of Nigerian traditional music and the arts
differentiate between the various types of festivals and dances
topics.content: General knowledge of the features and forms of Nigerian traditional music and other arts. Festivals: e.g. Osun, Ifa, Ogun, Ekpo, Ofala, Iriji (New Yam Festival), Ovia Osese, Mmanwu (Masquerade), Ila-Oso, Argungu (Fishing), Eyo/Adamu-Orisa, Gelede, etc. Dances and other arts (social, ritual and ceremonial): e.g. Masquerade, Koroso, Atilogwu, Ikperikpe (War dance), Egedeege, Kwaghir, Agbon, Nkwa Umuagbogho, Bata, Bori, Swange, Dundun, Kokoma, Abigbo, Okonko, etc.

topics.name: Nigerian traditional musical instruments
objectives: differentiate between the various types and classes of musical instruments
classify them into their categories
topics.content: Classifications of Nigerian traditional musical instruments.

classify aerophones: oja, opi, pipilo, udu, nnuk, ofiom, akpele, etc
classify aerophones: ekutu, teremagbe, ayeta-ode, odikakora, etc

subtopics.name: Chordophones
objectives: classify chordophones: goge, kukuma, komo, kwamsa, kuntigi, lasha, molo, garaya, gurmi, etc
classify chordophones: une, ubo-akwara, etc
classify chordophones: goje, molo, etc

objectives: classify idiophones: kundung, karawa, shantu, etc
classify idiophones: oyo, ichaka, ogene, aja, ekpili, ekwe, udu, ikoro, ngedegwu, okpokoro, ekere, mgbiligba, alo, ubo-aka, etc

subtopics.name: Membranophones
objectives: classify membranophones: ganga, tambari, taushi, banga, balle, kuntuku, kalangu, gangan-noma, tandu, etc
classify membranophones: igba, nsing, ban yogume, emoba, etc
classify membranophones: ipese, igbin, bata, bembe, gudugudu, kanango, dundun, gangan, etc

trace their biographies

topics.name: Historical development of Western music styles
objectives: trace the stages of the development of western musical practice from the medieval to the end of the romantic period
topics.content: Periods: Medieval/Middle Age (800-1400); Renaissance (1400-1600); Baroque (1600-1750); Classical (1750-1820); Romantic (1820-1900).

topics.name: Western composers
objectives: identify the composers
assess their contributions
topics.content: Palestrina, Claudio Monteverdi, Henry Purcell, J. S. Bach, G. F. Handel, W. A. Mozart, Franz Joseph Haydn, Ludwig van Beethoven, Franz Schubert, Frederic Chopin, etc.

topics.name: Music forms and media
objectives: identify the general forms and various types of instruments in Western music

topics.content: Binary, ternary, rondo, sonata allegro, dance suite, canon, free fantasia, theme and variation, etc; orchestral and band instruments and classifications; the human voice (its types, ranges and qualities); keyboard instruments (the organ, piano and electronic keyboard, etc); knowledge of the ukulele, banjo, guitar, mandolin, harp, accordion, xylophone, marimba, etc; computer music technology: software (Finale, Sibelius, Cubase, Reason, Sound Forge, Nero), tuning fork, pitch pipe, etc.
